claims.text: WVTaTiCr with Cr x=1 can be fabricated as a laser-cladded refractory multi-principal-element coating.
The as-cast or as-laser-cladded WVTaTiCr alloy has a BCC solid-solution matrix.
The initial alloy contains a network of Cr2Ta Laves precipitates and a coarse dendritic microstructure.
Cold rolling or severe plastic deformation followed by aging at 900°C for 5 minutes and 650°C for 20 hours is an applicable processing route for laser-cladded WVTaTiCr.
The 900°C treatment will form δ-lamellae in WVTaTiCr.
The subsequent 650°C treatment will form γ″ particles in WVTaTiCr.
The δ-lamellae and γ″ particles will have coherent interfaces with the BCC matrix.
The precipitates will have D0a and D022 structures and compositions similar to (Ni70Fe5)3(Ta20W5), or analogous Cr/Ta-rich compositions.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission, relieve stress concentrations, and thereby inhibit premature crack initiation.
The staged precipitates increase strength through order hardening and lattice-misfit strengthening.
A high density of grain boundaries and precipitates accelerates outward Cr and Ta diffusion and promotes a protective Cr2O3/TaO2/CrTaO4 layer.
Microstructural refinement suppresses non-protective spinel oxides and consequently improves both oxidation and aqueous-corrosion resistance.
The processed WVTaTiCr alloy will exceed 650 HV, compared with approximately 627.36 HV for the as-cladded Cr1 coating.
The proposed alloy and treatment will yield high density.
The processed WVTaTiCr alloy will have compressive strength above 1.5 GPa.
The processed alloy will have a corrosion rate below 0.1 mm/a in 3.5 wt% NaCl, versus 0.161 mm/a for the Cr1 baseline.
At 800°C, the treatment will reduce oxidation rate by more than 30% relative to the as-cast state; the stated Cr1 reference mass gain is 5.12 mg/cm² after 50 hours.
After treatment, the alloy will retain a single-phase or dual-phase BCC structure without brittle intermetallic fracture.
Aging above 900°C would cause the coherent precipitates to coarsen or transform into incoherent phases.
Cr content must remain at or above x=1.0 to form a protective Cr2O3 passive film.

contradictions.description: The initial and proposed treated microstructures explicitly include a Cr2Ta Laves network plus δ and γ″ precipitates, whereas the predicted outcome says the alloy will maintain a single-phase or dual-phase BCC structure. Unless those precipitates are excluded from the phase count, these descriptions are incompatible.

The mechanism deliberately introduces several ordered or intermetallic precipitate structures, while the boundary condition requires remaining in a BCC solid-solution region to avoid complex intermetallics; the acceptable amount or identity of intermetallic material is not reconciled.
